owners.description: ClaudeRuntimeCore owns the code-worker session lifecycle while the durable store and Web projection remain subordinate views.
PermissionApprovalRuntime owns approval continuation state and the audit runtime persists the canonical permission decision trail.
RetrievalIntegrationRuntime owns memory retrieval admission while commit, archive, and resume components preserve compact and restore semantics.
RecoveryApplication owns recovery orchestration and commits plans through the recovery store before route owners apply a recovery action.
LocalArtifactStore owns content-addressed artifact bytes and references while API and Web services provide policy-constrained projections.
WorkerPoolFoundationRuntime owns logical worker and lease state while the integration runtime commits physical dispatch and failover mutations.
GraphStateCustody owns immutable graph snapshots, branch-local mutations, conflict detection, commit lineage, and exact-resume checkpoints.
ProviderControlPlane owns provider, model, credential, dispatch, and failover coordination with a durable control-plane store.
McpRuntimeCoordinator owns MCP lifecycle coordination while its request journal and the skill registry preserve subordinate durable facts.
SandboxGatewayRuntime owns session and command lifecycle state with GatewayStateStore enforcing lease, busy, and recovery invariants.
TerminalSessionRegistry owns terminal sessions and BrowserSessionRuntime owns browser sessions as one explicitly shared interactive-session boundary.

requirements.description: A single run closes at least two thousand effective canonical state transitions without human intervention.
Memory retrieval, compact, restore, and skill memory change later context and decisions in a reproducible run.
Dynamic sparse topology mutates nodes and edges during one run and reports low-entropy comparison evidence.
The runtime demonstrates structured multi-agent communication with task, artifact, route, and causal event correlation.
Real local, isolated edge, and cloud dispatch provide privacy, latency, cost, and disconnected-degradation evidence.
Injected exceptions, requirement changes, node failures, and disconnects trigger observable recovery or deterministic replanning.
A visual causal trace links events to real state mutations, tools, artifacts, routes, verification, and recovery.
Submission documentation contains the core algorithm pseudocode, complexity analysis, architecture, and reproducible evidence map.
Long-horizon autonomous closed-loop completion score evidence.
Dynamic organization and topology score evidence.
Complex task breadth and completion quality score evidence.
Cross-domain live scenario coverage and completion score evidence.
Practical user value and artifact usefulness score evidence.
Interactive console usability and controllability score evidence.
Communication noise and topology entropy comparison score evidence.
Core algorithm rigor, pseudocode, and complexity analysis score evidence.
Fault tolerance, requirement-change handling, and node recovery score evidence.
Efficiency, latency, cost, and resource-use comparison score evidence.
Provider, model, operating-system, and runtime compatibility score evidence.
